newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen up at noon after FOMC stands pat.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen up at noon after FOMC stands pat.

text.p: The key three-month Euroyen deposit rate contract was moderately higher by midday in Tokyo on Wednesday following the decision by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Tuesday to keep interest rates steady.
"Euroyen futures were boosted in the morning as traders saw that there was no change in interest rates at the FOMC," said a brokerage trader.
"Earlier, about half the market had predicted the federal funds rate would rise by 0.25 percent, and this made traders wary of building long positions yesterday," the trader added.

The FOMC left the key federal funds rate, which banks charge each other for overnight loans, unchanged at 5-1/4 percent. It also left the discount rate, which the Fed charges banks, unchanged at five percent.
The FOMC's decision will probably have very little impact on the Bank of Japan's monetary policy, traders said.
The key three-month March Euroyen futures contract stood at 99.22 at midday, up from Tuesday's 99.18, after moving within a range of 99.20 to 99.23 in morning trade.
The BOJ drained 400 billion yen from the money market this morning, offsetting a projected fund surplus of 400 billion yen and maintaining its neutral money market stance.
Japan's key overnight call rate inched up to 0.49 percent in the morning from 0.48 percent on Tuesday.
"The overnight call rate is up because today is a bond settlement day," said a trust bank trader.
The weighted average for the overnight call rate probably will be 0.49 percent, although some players were trading at 0.50 percent, the trader said.
About 10 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) and 20 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were both issued at 0.53 percent.
One-month CDs were tagged with a sell quote of 0.52 percent.
All CD rates were unchanged from the previous day.
